To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BRCA1 and 2 are tumor suppressors whose function is to maintain genomic integrity by monitoring and repairing DNA damage.
the breast and ovarian cancer genes BRCA1 and 2 suppress tumorigenesis by controlling the assembly and function of multiprotein complexes that monitor the integrity of the genome.
BRCA1 and 2 are essential for the assembly and activity (but not the stability) of macromolecular protein complexes that control DNA replication, DNA repair, and chromosome segregation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of tumor suppression by the chromosome custodians, BRAC1 and BRAC2.
the fundamental mechanisms of genome stability and the role of these mechanisms in cancer.
the fundamental question of how cells maintain genome stability and how the failure to do so leads to cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“BRCA1 and BRC2 are the most important genes that protect us from cancer”.
BRCA proteins are the guardians of genome stability.
BRCA1 and 2 proteins are tumor suppressors that control chromosome integrity and that the inactivation of these proteins leads to cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BRCA proteins are guardians of the genome, and when they are lost, the genome is not guarded.
BRCA1 and 2 act as chromosome custodians and that their inactivation leads to cancer.
we have shown that the BRCA proteins are not tumor suppressors per se, but rather that their inactivation leads to the loss of a fundamental mechanism that prevents the development of tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BRCA proteins are essential guardians of genome integrity and that their loss is sufficient to initiate tumorigenesis.
BRCA1 and 2 are tumor suppressors by virtue of their roles in the assembly and activity, of macromolecular machines that monitor chromosome duplication and segregation.
BRCA1 and 2 are not tumor suppressors because they are involved in a particular DNA repair pathway, but because they are essential for the proper execution of the DNA damage response.
